question: No money bill can be introduced in the State Legislative Assembly without the prior permission of the ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A Money Bill can only be introduced in the State Legislative Assembly **with the prior permission of the Governor**.
 
• As per Article 207 of the Constitution of India, the Governor's recommendation is mandatory for introducing Money Bills in the State Legislature.
 
• The Money Bill deals with matters such as the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, or regulation of taxes, borrowing of money by the state, and matters related to the Consolidated Fund of the State.
 
• The Governor acts as the formal authority for legislative proposals involving state finances, ensuring they align with constitutional provisions.
 
• Without the Governor's recommendation, a Money Bill cannot proceed in the legislative process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Money Bill:**

 
 
• It is defined under Article 110 of the Indian Constitution (at the Union level) and Article 199 (at the State level).
 
• A Money Bill exclusively deals with financial matters like taxation, appropriation of funds, and public expenditure.
 
• It can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha (Union) or State Legislative Assembly (State) and requires prior recommendation from the President (Union) or Governor (State).
 
 
 
• **Role of the Governor:**
 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• In financial matters, the Governor ensures compliance with constitutional provisions by granting or withholding consent for legislative proposals.
 
 
 
• **State Legislature:**
 
 
• It comprises the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and, in some states, the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).
 
• The Legislative Assembly is the lower house where Money Bills are introduced and deliberated upon.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Process for Money Bills:**
 
 
• A Money Bill, after being introduced in the Legislative Assembly with the Governor's consent, goes through a detailed legislative process including debate, approval, and assent.
 
• The Legislative Council, if present, can only make recommendations and cannot amend or reject a Money Bill.
 
• After approval, it requires the Governor's assent to become law.
